title: A Asset for the Cover
premise: Orsen Kavanagh, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Office—an embassy that exists on no map—receives a meeting request from her handler, dead for six weeks. The invitation leads her into a conspiracy to stage a false-flag attack at an upcoming trilateral summit, designed to collapse a fragile arms treaty. Hunted by an assassin who knows her tradecraft because he trained beside her, Orsen must smuggle proof past three governments that all benefit from her silence. In the end she trades her own invisibility—her name, her cover, her freedom—for the truth, testifying publicly as the summit convenes and dismantling the Office from inside its own protocols.
about_author: Hazel Sterling is a former diplomatic security consultant who spent a decade advising missions she still cannot name. She writes thrillers from a coastal town whose location she declines to confirm.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Orsen Kavanagh, mid-routine cleanup of a compromised courier, receives a calendar invite from her handler Aldous Vey—dead six weeks. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: cold professional unease curdling into grief; the first crack in her belief that rules protect anyone.

chapters.title: Twelve Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Flashback-woven chapter establishing the Meridian Office's structure and Orsen's role erasing people. Her current handler, Brandt, questions her about the invite. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: belonging—the Office is the only family she has, and it just asked her a dangerous question.

chapters.title: Café Meridian
chapters.summary: Orsen keeps the meeting anyway. A dead-drop phone plays a recording: Vey's voice describing a staged attack at the summit, cut off mid-sentence. Someone watches from across the square. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose; loyalty to the dead over loyalty to the living institution.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Her to Vanish
chapters.summary: Introduce Cassian Roe, the Office's assassin, ordered to retrieve Orsen's evidence and, if necessary, retire her. POV: Roe. Emotional beat: reluctant respect—he recognizes her tradecraft as his own teaching, and hesitates one beat too long.

chapters.title: Protocol Seven
chapters.summary: Orsen runs counter-surveillance through Vienna while decoding Vey's message hidden in old operational files. She learns the false-flag op has a codename: COVERGLASS. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the thrill of competence shadowed by betrayal—someone inside fed Vey to the wolves.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Orsen approaches a treaty-delegation analyst, Ilse Marchetti, offering partial truth in exchange for summit access. POV: alternating Orsen/Ilse. Emotional beat: trust as a calculated gamble; two women deciding whether the other is worth burning for.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Roe corners Orsen at a safehouse but lets her go after she proves Vey was murdered by their own side. He takes half her evidence as insurance. POV: Roe. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh—he protects her not out of love but because killing her would end his only honest conversation.

chapters.title: What Vey Buried
chapters.summary: Decoded files reveal COVERGLASS targets a civilian delegation, with blame assigned to a third nation. The order bears Brandt's countersignature. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: vertigo—the family she belonged to authored the atrocity.

chapters.title: The Courier Who Didn't Run
chapters.summary: Orsen tries exfiltrating a witness, a junior officer who helped forge the documents. Roe's team intercepts them; the witness dies buying Orsen ten minutes. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: guilt hardening into resolve; justice outside the law now has a body count.

chapters.title: Brandt's Table
chapters.summary: Summoned to headquarters, Orsen sits across from Brandt, who offers promotion and full restoration of her identity if she surrenders the files. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: temptation—belonging offered as a bribe—and her quiet refusal.

chapters.title: Ilse's Price
chapters.summary: Marchetti agrees to get Orsen into the summit perimeter but demands the story run under her byline, exposing both governments' complicity. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: ambition entangled with conscience; neither woman fully trusts the other, and both proceed.

chapters.title: Roe's Ledger
chapters.summary: Roe audits his own kill history and finds three targets whose deaths served COVERGLASS's architecture—including, possibly, Vey's. POV: Roe. Emotional beat: horror of self-recognition; the instrument discovering what it was built to build.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: A handoff goes wrong; Orsen is captured by an interagency task force that wants COVERGLASS buried as much as the Office does. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: claustrophobic despair—three governments closing like a fist.

chapters.title: The Interrogation Room
chapters.summary: A coalition spymaster offers Orsen asylum in exchange for silence until 'after the summit.' She realizes they plan to let the attack happen and exploit it. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: clarity through betrayal; there is no institutional exit, only hers.

chapters.title: Extraction, Unsanctioned
chapters.summary: Roe burns his own network to pull Orsen out, going rogue for the first time in twenty years. POV: Roe. Emotional beat: redemption through treason; the loyalist finally choosing a person over a flag.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Fugitives in Prague, Orsen and Roe assemble the full chain of evidence and a plan to breach the summit media center before the opening session. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: wary intimacy between two people trained never to need anyone.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: They identify the insider who betrayed Vey: not Brandt, but the Office's archivist, who engineered everything to force the treaty's collapse for private buyers. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: fury refined into focus; the enemy finally has a face.

chapters.title: Perimeter
chapters.summary: Infiltration night. Ilse gets them press credentials; Roe neutralizes the assassin team sent as backup-killers. POV: alternating trio. Emotional beat: taut coordination—trust operating at speed, no time for doubt.

chapters.title: COVERGLASS
chapters.summary: Climax: as delegates convene, Orsen reaches the broadcast control room and forces the evidence onto every screen while the archivist triggers the attack early. Roe stops the trigger man; Brandt, arriving to contain the leak, sees the truth live and stands down. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the whole book compressed—one woman refusing to be erased.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Orsen surrenders voluntarily and testifies publicly, naming names including her own operations. Governments scramble; the treaty survives because exposure forced honesty. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: costly vindication—justice achieved by giving up every protection she had.

chapters.title: What the Office Was For
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the Meridian Office is dissolved; Brandt faces inquiry; Ilse's reporting reshapes the summit's final accords. Roe vanishes, leaving Orsen a single untraceable note. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude braided together; institutions fall, people remain.

chapters.title: A Name on the Door
chapters.summary: Months later, Orsen lives openly under her real name, consulting for treaty verification—a legal version of her old work. A new invitation arrives from an unknown sender. She smiles, and this time chooses whether to answer. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: earned peace with an open door; belonging now chosen, not assigned.
